knowledge:
- key_parameters: type=Specifies whether the NGS experiment contains "paired" or "single" end read fragments ;; fragmentLen=Maximum length of reads to keep (e.g., 200bp to discard extra long reads in paired-end mononucleosome data) ;; trim=Number of bases to keep around the dyad (e.g., trim=40) to increase sharpness ;; pcKeepComp=Percentage of components to keep in Fourier space (e.g., 0.01 for Tiling Arrays, 0.02 for NGS) to remove noise ;; threshold=Threshold value for detecting peaks (e.g., "25%") ;; width=Width of the nucleosome (e.g., 140) to account for fuzziness/sharpness in scoring
- alternatives: Hidden Markov Models (HMMs), Support Vector Machines (SVMs), or higher-order Bayesian Networks are mentioned as complex alternatives for dealing with noise and fuzzy positioning, whereas nucleR offers a simpler, faster FFT-based peak calling method.
- when_to_use: Use when analyzing nucleosome positioning experiments (ChIP-seq or ChIP-on-Chip) to identify, score, and visualize well-positioned and fuzzy nucleosomes.
- pitfalls: Avoid simple sliding window averages for smoothing as they can shift peak positions and shapes; do not set threshold to 0 in peakDetection to avoid detecting minor noise fluctuations; note that coverage.rpm can yield extremely high values on small subset datasets because it scales to millions of reads.

workflows.name: ngs_nucleosome_calling
workflows.intent: Process NGS BAM files to call, score, and plot nucleosome positions.
input: cellCycleM_chrII_5000-25000.bam (BAM file containing mapped NGS reads)
workflows.stages: 1. Import BAM file using readBAM ;; 2. Process and trim reads using processReads ;; 3. Calculate normalized coverage using coverage.rpm ;; 4. Smooth coverage signal using filterFFT ;; 5. Detect and score peaks using peakDetection ;; 6. Plot peaks using plotPeaks
workflows.code:
sample.file <- system.file("extdata", "cellCycleM_chrII_5000-25000.bam",
    package="nucleR")
reads <- readBAM(sample.file, type="paired")
reads_pair <- processReads(nucleosome_htseq, type="paired", fragmentLen=200)
reads_trim <- processReads(nucleosome_htseq, type="paired", fragmentLen=200,
    trim=40)
cover_pair <- coverage.rpm(reads_pair)
cover_trim <- coverage.rpm(reads_trim)
htseq_raw <- as.vector(cover_trim[[1]])
htseq_fft <- filterFFT(htseq_raw, pcKeepComp=0.02)
peaks <- peakDetection(htseq_fft, threshold="25%", score=FALSE)
plotPeaks(peaks, htseq_fft, threshold="25%", ylab="coverage")
peaks <- peakDetection(htseq_fft, threshold="25%", score=TRUE)
plotPeaks(peaks, htseq_fft, threshold="25%")
peaks <- peakDetection(htseq_fft, threshold="25%", score=TRUE, width=140)
plotPeaks(peaks, htseq_fft, threshold="25%")

workflows.name: tiling_array_nucleosome_calling
workflows.intent: Process Tiling Array fluorescence intensities to call and score nucleosome positions.
input: tiling_data.RData (ExpressionSet or numeric vector of normalized fluorescence intensities)
workflows.stages: 1. Process tiling array data to 1bp resolution using processTilingArray ;; 2. Smooth signal using filterFFT ;; 3. Detect peaks using peakDetection
workflows.code:
processTilingArray(data, exprName, chrPattern, inferLen=50)
data(nucleosome_tiling)
fft_ta <- filterFFT(nucleosome_tiling, pcKeepComp=0.01, showPowerSpec=TRUE)
tiling_raw <- nucleosome_tiling
tiling_fft <- filterFFT(tiling_raw, pcKeepComp=0.01)

workflows.name: mnase_bias_correction
workflows.intent: Correct nucleosomal DNA coverage profiles using a mock control sample of naked DNA digested with MNase.
workflows.code:
map <- syntheticNucMap(as.ratio=TRUE, wp.num=50, fuz.num=25)
exp <- coverage(map$syn.reads)
ctr <- coverage(map$ctr.reads)
corrected <- controlCorrection(exp, ctr)
